trans-unit.target: Completed entries remain editable. Removed deductions are not reapplied.
Calculated deductions do not prove that a break was taken.
Use distinct thresholds, non-decreasing break totals and valid interruption lengths.
Calculates a break once, when an entry is first completed. Running timers are unchanged. Completed entries are not recalculated; their breaks can still be corrected.
Choose 1–10 rules. Saving a lower count removes the last rules. Increasing it again before saving restores temporarily hidden values.
Recorded time within a work block, before deducting breaks. At a 360-minute threshold, 6:00:00 triggers no deduction; 6:00:01 does. Clock-out gaps are excluded. Each rule needs a distinct threshold.
The total break for this rule. A first rule of 30 minutes and a second of 45 require at most 45 minutes, not 75. Existing breaks are credited. Break totals must not decrease as thresholds increase.

0 disables the daily cap and preserves longer working times. A positive value deducts excess net time as a break, including across multiple work blocks. Example: a 600-minute limit would produce 14 hours of total break in a 24-hour entry. This setting does not issue a warning.

A clock-out gap of at least this duration resets the break-rule counter. With 15 minutes configured, four hours of work, a 15-minute gap and another four hours form two blocks. 0 combines all blocks until the next workday. This does not check whether the total daily rest break is sufficient.

A gap of at least this duration starts a new accounting workday. 660 minutes equals 11 hours. Midnight alone does not reset the counters. The value must be positive and at least as long as the block-reset gap. This does not validate statutory rest periods.
Members of any selected team receive no automatic deductions, including for other projects or additional team memberships. The exemption applies to the entire person, not just work for that team.
Your recorded time in the work block exceeds %threshold%. The configured break rules automatically added %added% of break time to your entry.
You exceeded the maximum working time of %threshold% per workday. %added% of break time was therefore added automatically to your entry.

Fixed deduction: the entire break total is required immediately above the threshold. Maximum deduction: deduct only the excess above the threshold, up to the configured total. Example 360 / 30: at 6:15, fixed deducts 30 minutes and maximum deducts 15. Earlier rule totals remain credited.

Add rules with + and remove them with −. Rules are sorted automatically by threshold. Break amounts are totals: 30 and 45 minutes require at most 45 minutes. Changes apply to entries completed from now on.
A block reset does not check the total daily rest break. The workday boundary is an accounting grouping, not a rest-period check. Deducting excess working time cannot replace taking a real break.

Automatic Breaks is currently inactive because breaks are disabled in Kimai. Enable Breaks under System → Settings → Time tracking to allow automatic deductions. Your rules are saved, but they will only apply when both breaks and this plugin are enabled.
